metric_rationale: In trials 1 and 2, one option has the two highest validity features (0.9 and 0.85) while the other option has the three lowest validity features (0.6, 0.55, 0.5). Tallying will robustly choose the option with three features (since 3 > 2), completely ignoring the cardinal validities. In contrast, WADD integrates cardinal validities and will generally prefer the option with the two highest validity features, because 0.9 + 0.85 > 0.6 + 0.55 + 0.5. This metric isolated these critical trials and calculates the proportion of times the subject chooses the Tallying-predicted option. Tallying will yield a high value, whereas WADD will yield a low value.

This metric calculates the proportion of times the subject chooses the option with the first two (highly valid) features over the option with the last three (less valid) features. Tallying strictly prefers the option with three features (score approaches 0), whereas WADD, on average, assigns a higher weighted sum to the two highly valid features (score > 0.5). Thus, this specific trial type perfectly dissociates the two models.

In all 6 trial types, the Take-The-Best (TTB) model will deterministically select Option A because Option A always has the advantage on the highest-validity cue that discriminates the two options. In contrast, the Weighted Additive (WADD) model integrates all cues, and in most of these trials, Option B has a higher sum of weighted validities (compensatory advantage from multiple lower-validity cues). Therefore, the overall proportion of choosing Option A will be near 1.0 for TTB and much lower for WADD.

We measure the proportion of choices that align with the Take-The-Best (TTB) heuristic. Because the experiment consists mostly of 'compensatory' trials where WADD and TTB predict opposite responses (e.g., one option wins on the single most valid cue, while the other wins on several less valid cues that together outweigh the first), this metric will be high for data generated by TTB and low for data generated by WADD.

Strategy Mixture Theory posits that individuals mix between TTB and Tallying on a trial-by-trial basis. On conflict trials where the two heuristics disagree, an SMT agent will stochasticly alternate between the two options across repetitions of the exact same trial, yielding a choice proportion near 0.5 (low extremity). In contrast, WADD computes a deterministic weighted sum based on subjective validities. For any specific trial, a WADD agent will consistently favor one option over the other across all repetitions (modulo some response noise), yielding choice proportions closer to 0 or 1 (high extremity). By measuring the absolute deviation of the intra-individual choice proportion from 0.5 on identical conflict trials, we can cleanly separate the stochastic strategy mixing of SMT from the deterministic weighting of WADD.

This metric computes the difference in the probability of choosing Option A between Trial 2 and Trial 4. In both of these trials, the Strategy Mixture model pits Take-The-Best (which chooses A) against Tallying (which chooses B), resulting in a predicted choice proportion for A equal to the mixing parameter `p_ttb` (around 0.50) in both cases, making the expected difference 0. However, the Weighted Additive (WADD) model strongly differentiates the two trials: Option A in Trial 2 has an additional high-validity feature compared to Option A in Trial 4, while Option B remains identical. Consequently, WADD predicts a substantially higher choice probability for A in Trial 2 than in Trial 4. This difference will be positive and large under WADD, but zero under Strategy Mixture.
